statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The opening decline has been fully retraced: NDX is 29,126.69 (-0.62%) at 16:26Z, back above its 29,094.72 open and within 17 points of the 29,143.52 session high, some 251 points off the 28,875.97 low. NQ is 29,164.75 at 16:05Z against a 28,948.00 low. VIX is 15.69 at the low end of a 15.62-16.06 range. Tail is in the low band; Stress stays elevated on a memory-led de-rating and the pending Treasury announcement on Iran, with the danger window narrowed to 16:50Z-19:00Z.
recommendation: Descriptive: the structure that raised Tail around the cash open was a failed floor with only a 32-point pullback. It has now been completely invalidated. The cash index has retraced the entire 218.75-point opening range and trades above the open, which is the opposite of the no-retracement path that overwhelms a mean-reversion basket. Volatility is decaying rather than expanding, with VIX 15.69 near the bottom of its day range and VIX futures lower. Cross-assets do not confirm an equity stress event: the 10-year yield is 4.3bp lower at 4.69%, the 2-year is unchanged at 4.24%, Treasury futures are bid across the curve and oil is more than 2% lower. Breadth is a rotation rather than a liquidation, with the Dow higher, the S&P near flat and five of eight megacaps positive against a semiconductor complex down more than 3%. Tail is therefore scored at 10. Stress remains at 50 because the memory de-rating is large, the Treasury press conference on Iran sanctions at 17:00Z is unresolved, and Nvidia reports on Wednesday. The danger window covers the announcement and its immediate reaction only.
headline: Nasdaq-100: the opening decline is fully retraced and volatility is decaying, so Tail stays low while Stress holds elevated into the 17:00Z Iran announcement
body:
The recovery flagged an hour ago has completed. The Nasdaq-100 cash index is 29,126.69 (-0.62%) at 16:26Z on Investing.com real-time data, above its 29,094.72 open and 17 points below the 29,143.52 session high, having traded as low as 28,875.97. That is a full retracement of the opening range and then some. NQ futures confirm the shape at 29,164.75 at 16:05Z on Yahoo Finance, roughly 217 points above the 28,948.00 low inside a 28,948.00-29,480.50 day range. The failed-floor structure that justified an elevated Tail reading at 14:00Z no longer exists.

Volatility agrees. VIX is 15.69 (+3.70%) against a 15.62-16.06 day range and a 15.13 previous close, so it sits at the low end of the range it made this morning, and Finviz VIX futures context is 0.58% lower. The move is decay, not expansion.

Cross-assets are not aligned with an equity stress event. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.69%, 4.3bp lower on the day, and the 2-year is 4.24%, effectively unchanged; delayed Treasury futures context shows the whole curve bid, with the 30-year contract up 0.72%. WTI is about 85.00 dollars, more than 2% lower, and Brent about 92.43 dollars, as traders take profit on a two-week rally while waiting for the sanctions detail. Falling oil alongside falling yields is not the signature of a risk-liquidation path in equities.

The day's weakness is narrow and thematic. The Philadelphia semiconductor index is down more than 3% and memory names lead the decline, with Micron, SanDisk, Seagate and Western Digital each off more than 5%, after a report that Nvidia will raise AI-server prices by more than 15% early next year because of surging memory costs, and separate reporting that Apple may source memory from Chinese suppliers. Against that, the Dow is higher, the S&P 500 is near flat, and delayed Finviz context shows five of eight megacaps positive with Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Apple all higher while Nvidia, Broadcom and Tesla are lower. Internal dispersion of that kind is a rotation, and rotations supply the two-way trade a mean-reversion basket depends on.

The unresolved item is scheduled rather than observed. Reuters places the Treasury press conference on new Iran sanctions at 17:00Z, and the Treasury press-release page carries nothing from today, so no outcome exists yet. One earlier report placed the conference an hour later, which is why the danger window extends to 19:00Z rather than closing immediately after the opening remarks. Secondary sanctions aimed at buyers of Iranian oil are the plausible transmission channel, and the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, so a genuine supply discontinuity is possible. Under the calibration in force, a pending event of that kind raises Stress and shortens the evidence horizon; it does not by itself establish the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures.

The forecast therefore holds the low Tail band across all 24 hours, stepping to 16 and 17 across the announcement window, easing overnight, and lifting again to 17 at the Tuesday cash open where CB Consumer Confidence and New Home Sales print at 14:00Z. Confidence is 86: live cash and futures quotes, a live volatility reading, current yields and oil, fresh cross-asset context and a verified calendar are all in hand, and the only material uncertainty is the one-hour discrepancy in the reported press-conference time.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Through the 23 August afternoon and evening Tail was pinned at 4 with the EA_ON mapping while Stress drifted from 39 to 45 in a normal mode. Tail stepped to 15 at 22:00Z as the Asian technology decline began, then settled into a 7-12 band overnight. It rose to 19 at 07:00Z with Stress at 58 as the European session priced the memory complex lower in a trend-down mode, eased to 11-13 in a mixed mode through the European morning, moved to 20 at 13:00Z with the cash open pending, and reached 26 at 14:00Z, the only slot in the window mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES, when the index sat near its low with a single shallow pullback. It fell back to 13 at 15:00Z as that structure failed and the retracement began. The window therefore contains one short orange slot and one yellow slot inside an otherwise green series, and the elevated reading was resolved by observed mean reversion rather than by extension.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds the low Tail band through every hour of the forecast. It steps to 16 at 17:00Z and 17 at 18:00Z around the Treasury announcement on Iran sanctions, which is scored as Stress and event risk because no post-announcement price path has been observed, then eases to 14 at 19:00Z and 12 into the 20:00Z cash close. Conditional Stress peaks at 56 in the announcement window and decays through the evening to a 40-45 overnight floor. The series lifts to 14 at the Tokyo and Seoul opens, where the memory complex is repriced directly, and to 13 at the European cash open. It then builds through the Tuesday European afternoon to 14 at 13:00Z with Case-Shiller pending and 17 at 14:00Z, the highest conditional slot, where the US cash open coincides with CB Consumer Confidence and New Home Sales, before easing to 15 at 15:00Z. Confidence declines gradually from 86 to 75 across the horizon as the forecast moves beyond currently observed evidence.
